name: Land Between the Rivers
inspired_by: Central and northern Iraq as of 2026: the Tigris alluvial plain with date palm groves and irrigation canals, the Jazira and Anbar desert to the west toward the Syrian border, the Hamrin hills and oil-rich disputed foothills to the north-east, and the first Zagros ranges of the Kurdistan Region in the far north-east corner. US forces left federal Iraq by 30 September 2026; ISIS persists as rural cells. All towns are fictional.
climate: Hot desert to semi-arid (Koppen BWh in the south and west, BSh in the north-east). Summers 44-50 C on the plain, among the hottest inhabited places on earth; winters 5-16 C with frost at night; 100-200 mm rain on the plain, up to 500 mm in the foothills, falling November-April.
seasons: Winter (Dec-Feb): cool, rain turns farm tracks and riverbanks to mud, morning fog in the palm groves
Spring (Mar-May): wheat harvest, frequent dust storms, rising heat
Summer (Jun-Sep): extreme heat, haze, low river levels, power cuts
Autumn (Oct-Nov): date harvest, cooling, first rains in the north

vegetation: date palm (Phoenix dactylifera) groves with citrus and pomegranate understorey
Euphrates poplar and willow on banks
grassland and wheat on rolling hills
walnut and pomegranate orchards in valleys

terrain.relief: Very flat alluvial plain (40-80 m) across the centre and south, with raised canal levees and river banks the only relief; a low desert plateau rising west to 250 m with wadis and escarpments; the Hamrin ridge (300-500 m) crossing the north-east; foothills and the first Zagros ranges climbing to 1,300 m in the far north-east.
features: meandering Tigris-type river with levees and islands
dense canal network with earth embankments
a large shallow lake/depression at the west edge
oil field pads, pipelines and flares
terrain.water: One large river (200-400 m) meandering north-west to south-east, a tributary from the north-east foothills, a barrage with locks, hundreds of canals and drains, a shallow desert lake at the west edge, marsh patches in the south-east corner.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 10 m. Mostly flat base with a westward desert rise and a north-east foothill ramp; river carved as a meandering spline with levees (raised 2-4 m) built up on both banks; canals are a procedural network branching off the river (Lindenmayer-style tree, 1-12 m wide, with embankments). Ridges via anisotropic noise masked to the north-east.

noise_layers.purpose: west desert rise and north-east foothill rise; plain stays at 40-80 m
Hamrin ridge and Zagros front ranges, masked to the north-east third
salinity mask: converts some fields to bare salt crust

generator.erosion: Hydraulic erosion only on the desert plateau and foothills; the plain is kept flat (no erosion) and shaped by levees and canals.
generator.rivers: Main river spline with meander amplitude 1-2 km and levees; tributary from the north-east; canals branch from the river and the barrage and end in drains; wadis on the plateau from flow accumulation.
generator.settlement_flattening: Settlements on the plain sit on levees or slightly raised mounds; flatten with 40 m skirts. Foothill villages per plot.
generator.notes: On the flat plain, palm groves and canal embankments are the only cover and break line of sight to 50-200 m: ideal ambush and IED-hazard terrain. Bridges over the river (4) and the barrage are convoy chokepoints; canals block vehicles except at culverts and small bridges.

settlements.architecture: Plain villages in the palm groves: one- and two-storey houses of fired yellow brick or cinder block with flat roofs and parapets, walled yards with metal gates, rooftop water tanks and satellite dishes; a few older mud-brick houses; a mosque or husseiniya with a green or blue dome.
settlements.wall_class: Fired-brick walls 24-36 cm medium; yard walls 25 cm medium; cinder-block additions thin; mud brick thick.
layout_rules: strung along a canal or levee road
houses inside palm groves with tracks between
mosque at the junction with a small shop row
canal bridges and culverts as the only vehicle crossings

settlements.architecture: River town: two- to four-storey fired-brick and concrete buildings with flat roofs, older houses with wooden shanasheel bay windows in the old quarter, arcaded market streets, a large shrine or mosque with a gold or blue dome, government buildings behind T-walls, a riverside corniche.
settlements.wall_class: Brick medium; concrete frames thick; T-walls around government sites thick.
layout_rules: old quarter of lanes on the riverbank
market street and a main mosque or shrine as landmark
T-wall compounds for government and security buildings

settlements.architecture: Kurdistan Region city district in the north-east: four- to twelve-storey concrete buildings with stone and glass facades, malls, a citadel mound, hotels and compounds for foreign missions, a sprawl of two-storey villas.
settlements.wall_class: Concrete frames thick; glass none; compound walls thick.
layout_rules: ring roads around a central citadel mound
hotel and consulate district with walls
airport and coalition advisory compound on the edge

settlements.architecture: Farm compounds: a two-storey house, a reed-and-mud livestock shed, a pump house on the canal, hay stacks, a high wall.
settlements.wall_class: Compound wall mud or brick 30-40 cm thick; sheds thin.
layout_rules: on a canal bank, one access track
palm grove on one side, fields on the other

settlements.architecture: Security, military and oil sites: ISF bases in former Coalition bases (T-walls, HESCO, guard towers, hangar tents), oil field gathering stations and refineries, a power station, Peshmerga hilltop posts, a militia base in a walled former farm.
settlements.wall_class: T-walls, HESCO and berms thick; prefabs and tents none.
layout_rules: T-wall perimeter with entry control point and serpentine

infrastructure.roads: A four-lane north-south highway along the river (with overpasses and checkpoints), an older two-lane river road, desert highways west to the Syrian and Jordanian borders, canal-bank tracks in the groves, mountain roads in the north-east. Four river bridges and a barrage road are chokepoints.
infrastructure.rail: Single-track line north-south with a station, sidings at the refinery, and a broken bridge.
infrastructure.power: Thermal power station and a refinery on the river, 400 kV lines across the plain, generators everywhere; frequent outages.
infrastructure.airfields: An ex-Coalition air base with long runways and hangars (ISF), a KRG civil airport in the north-east (coalition advisory presence), agricultural strips.
infrastructure.checkpoints: ISF checkpoints at highway junctions, bridges and town entrances (T-walls, a shelter, flags); PMF-badged posts on some roads (state forces, not the hostile faction); Peshmerga checkpoints on the disputed-area line; border crossings at the west edge.

pois.description: Weapons and explosives cache buried in a palm grove beside a canal, marked by a rag on a tree; a small hut with a generator nearby. IED-hazard tracks around it.
ISIS cell hideout in Hamrin hill gullies: dug-outs covered with tarps and scrub, a motorbike, food and water stores, an observation post on the crest.
pois.contract_use: desert hideout clearance; HVT capture (client irq, krg_peshmerga)

pois.description: Steel truss bridge with an ISF checkpoint at each end, T-walls and a fuel station; the river road passes beneath through palm groves.
Oil gathering station and pipeline junction in the foothills: tanks, separators, flare, a pump house, workers' prefabs, berm and towers.
pois.contract_use: escort oil convoy; protect infrastructure; drone defence (clients irq, krg_peshmerga)

pois.description: Walled farm used by a militia drone and rocket team: launch rails hidden in a shed, a pickup, crates, a generator and a lookout. Map hazard: unexploded rockets.
pois.contract_use: recover launch-site intel for a client; defend a site it targets

pois.description: Large base handed to the ISF: hangars, T-wall streets, empty accommodation blocks, a runway; partly abandoned.
pois.contract_use: staging; recover lost equipment or sensitive kit left behind

pois.description: Wadi crossing the western desert with a smuggling track, an abandoned police post and a burnt tanker; the route to the Syrian border.
River barrage with sluice gates, a road across the top, lock chambers and a control building; reed islands upstream.
Peshmerga post on a ridge overlooking disputed villages: sandbagged positions, a container, a flag, a dirt road.

pois.description: Busy market around a domed shrine, arcades, pilgrims, blast walls at the entrances.
pois.contract_use: VIP protection; counter-terror security during a pilgrimage (high civilian density)

pois.description: Village emptied in the 2014-2017 war: damaged houses, booby-trap hazard markers, overgrown groves; used by cells as a waypoint.

conditions: dust storms (haboob and shamal) in spring and summer

weather.visibility_notes: Dust storms bring visibility under 100 m for hours and ground helicopters and drones; summer heat shimmer; palm groves limit sight to 50-200 m in any weather.
weather.dust_or_snow: Dust frequent from March to August; snow only in the north-east ranges in winter.

civilians.behaviour: Farmers in fields and groves at dawn; markets 07:00-12:00 and evening; summer afternoons nearly empty; Friday prayers fill mosques at midday; pilgrim crowds around the shrine town on religious dates. Civilians recognise IED-hazard signs and avoid them; after shooting they shelter in walled yards. Herders with sheep and Bedouin in the desert.
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: Towns, the shrine market and grove villages are dense; desert and Hamrin zones are nearly empty and suit hard fights.

frontline: Two dynamics. (1) Counter-isis: isis cells regenerate in the Hamrin hills and western wadis and push into abandoned and grove villages at night; ISF and Peshmerga sweeps (and player contracts) push them back. A cell that survives three campaign days in a zone flips it to 'contested' and starts IED hazards on its roads. (2) Militia pressure: iraqi_militias launch drone and rocket attacks on oil sites, the KRG city and foreign compounds; each attack raises their zones' alert and posts site-defence contracts, while disarmament events (campaign calendar, deadline mid-2027) lower their strength. ISF never fights PMF-badged state units; contracts never target them. Peshmerga-ISF relations shift the disputed-area line only through political events (no combat between them).
contract_hooks: ISIS cell raid on a Hamrin gully hideout (clients irq, krg_peshmerga)
Palm grove cache raid with IED-hazard approaches (clients irq, usa, gbr)
Escort an oil convoy from the foothill station to the refinery over a river bridge (client irq)
Defend an oil or gas site against militia drone and rocket attacks (client krg_peshmerga)
HVT capture of an isis emir in an abandoned village (clients irq, fra, usa)
Reinforce the border detention camp against a breakout attempt (clients sdf, irq)
Recover sensitive kit left at an ex-Coalition base before militias loot it (clients usa, gbr, pol)
Train and accompany a Peshmerga brigade on a night sweep (clients krg_peshmerga, deu, ita)
Escort a VIP convoy between the KRG city and a border town (client krg_peshmerga)

hot_zones.name: Disputed foothills
hot_zones.layout: isis HQ in an abandoned village; 4-5 outposts in gullies and ridge caves; isis checkpoints on two tracks at night; motorbike patrols; 1 QRF of pickups and technicals; Peshmerga and ISF posts on the edges as allies

hot_zones.name: Grove belt
hot_zones.layout: iraqi_militias HQ in a walled farm; 3-4 launch sites as outposts; checkpoints on canal bridges; roaming pickups and drone teams; 1 QRF of Land Cruisers

insertion.fob: FOB inside an ISF-held ex-Coalition base on the plain (helipad, workshops). Alternative FOB at the KRG airport for north-east contracts. Players reach zones by highway, canal-bank tracks or helicopter; AAVs can cross canals but not the foothill ranges.

early_game_notes: isis and iraqi_militias are early-tier; Hamrin and grove contracts are the core early-game loop with many friendly clients (irq, krg_peshmerga, sdf, Western states).
